lead.t: Neurodevelopmental: intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD.

b: Definition: persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction , together with restricted, repetitive patterns of behaviour, interests or activities, present from early childhood.
Poor eye contact, no response to name by 12 months.
No babbling, pointing or gestures by 12 months; no words by 16 months ; no spontaneous two-word phrases by 24 months .
Loss of language or social skills at any age.
Lack of pretend play ; lining up toys; hand-flapping or other stereotypies; insistence on sameness; unusual sensory responses (to sound, touch or texture).

snip.t: The most common neurologic manifestations of TSC consist of epilepsy, cognitive impairment, and autism spectrum disorder.
45% of individuals with TSC have intellectual disability, and up to 50% have autism spectrum disorder.

qs.q: A pediatrician evaluates an infant during a routine 12-month well-child visit for early behavioral signs of autism spectrum disorder. Which finding represents the earliest recognizable red flag?
o: Failure to respond to own name
Lack of peer interactive play skills
Loss of spoken words at age three
qs.e: Failure to respond to one's name by 12 months is one of the earliest social-communication red flags for autism. The other listed features typically become apparent much later in toddlerhood or childhood.

qs.q: Which medication is indicated for severe irritability in autism spectrum disorder?
qs.e: Risperidone is used for irritability in ASD. The other drugs treat ADHD or depression.
